title: Lesson 5: Close Read-aloud, Session 3 and Role-Playing: Summer Sun Risin'
objective: Students will describe what the boy and the sun do in the middle of the story Summer Sun Risin' through close reading, role-playing, discussion, and writing.

what_is_taught.skill: identify nouns and verbs in a song
recognize and identify pronouns replacing nouns
describe story elements including main character, setting, and events
use key details from text to describe what characters do
participate in role-playing to act out story events
reflect on and discuss respectful behavior during partner work
write and draw about story events using sentence frames
use sentence stems to support oral expression
engage in structured discussion using Think-Pair-Share protocol

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify nouns, verbs, and pronouns in a song and story
student_actions.oral_production: participate in partner discussions, role-play, and whole group sharing
student_actions.written_production: write and draw about story events using sentence frames
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain what the boy and sun do and how respect is shown
student_actions.comprehension_response: respond to questions about story elements and experiences with the sun during midday and other times of day

evidence.quote: Direct students' attention to the ' Sun, Moon, and Stars' Version 2 song and invite them to join you in singing.
Remind students that this song uses nouns and their matching verbs. Remind students that nouns are people, places, or things (like 'the sun'!), and that verbs are action words (like 'shines'!).
'What are some of the nouns and verbs that go together in this song?' (Responses will vary)
Tell students that not only does this song use nouns and verbs, it also includes pronouns. Tell students that a pronoun is a word that can take the place of a noun.

Redirect students' attention to the first verse and reread it aloud. Tell students that the pronoun in this verse is 'it' because it replaces the noun 'the sun'. Use a marker to draw a box around the pronoun 'it'.
Tell students that you are slowly going to repeat the song. When they hear or see a pronoun they can touch their nose.
Sing the song aloud slowly and draw a box around the pronouns.
After singing the song and drawing a box around the pronouns and invite students to reread the pronouns with you: 'it' and 'them'.
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner: 'Who is the main character? Where does the story take place? What happened in the beginning of the story?'
Refocus whole group and invite one or two students to share out.
Direct students' attention to the posted learning target and read it aloud: 'I can describe what the boy and the sun do in the middle of Summer Sun Risin'.'
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner:
'Where do you think the sun will be in the middle of the story?'
Guide students through the close read-aloud for Summer Sun Risin' using the Close Readaloud Guide: Summer Sun Risin' (Session 3; for teacher reference).
Refocus students whole group.
Offer specific feedback on their close reading skills used to explore the focus question: 'What is the boy doing when the sun is at its highest in the sky?'

Tell students that later in the lesson they will write and draw about the beginning and middle events so today they will continue to think about, discuss, and role-play these events with a partner so they better understand them in order to do their best writing.
Move students into pre-determined pairs and tell them they are going to use the Role-Play protocol to act out a few of the middle events of Summer Sun Risin'.
Remind students to focus on showing respect while working with a partner during the RolePlay protocol.
Invite students to begin the Role-Play protocol for the following sections of text:

Tell students that in the next lesson, they will role-play the ending events from the story and use their thinking from this role-play to help with writing and drawing about the major events from the story.
Tell students they are going to use the Think-Pair-Share protocol to discuss how they showed respect during the Role-Play protocol.
'What did it look and sound like when you were showing respect during the Role-Play protocol?'
Invite them to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner: 'What did it look and sound like when you were showing respect during the Role-Play protocol?'
Gather students back together and invite a few students to share out.
Display Part II of the Summer Sun Risin' response sheet.

Read the directions aloud: 'Draw a picture to show an event from the beginning of the story, from the middle of the story, and from the end of the story. Complete the sentence frame at the bottom of each box to tell what your picture shows.'
Invite students to turn and talk to an elbow partner:
Invite students to show a thumbs-up or touch their head if they are ready to begin writing and drawing about the events from the beginning and middle of Summer Sun Risin'.
Transition students to their workspaces and invite them to begin.
Circulate and support students as necessary. Encourage them to use classroom resources (Word Walls, high-frequency word lists, and alphabet or letter sound combination charts) as necessary.
After 5 minutes, signal students to stop working. Model cleanup, keeping directions clear and brief.
Gather students together whole group.

Tell them they are going to use the Think-Pair-Share protocol to discuss what the boy experiences when the sun is highest in the sky and what they themselves experience when the sun is highest in the sky.
Invite students to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner: 'Where is the sun during midday?'
'What does the boy experience during midday?'
'What do you experience during midday?'
Gather students back together and invite a few students to share with the whole group.

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Models identification of nouns, verbs, and pronouns in a song; models close reading of text; models role-play and respectful partner behavior; models use of sentence frames for writing; models Think-Pair-Share discussion protocol.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What are some of the nouns and verbs that go together in this song?
Who is the main character? Where does the story take place? What happened in the beginning of the story?
What time of day do you think the middle of the story takes place?
Where do you think the sun will be in the middle of the story?
What did it look and sound like when you were showing respect during the Role-Play protocol?
Where is the sun during midday?
What does the boy experience during midday?
What do you experience during midday?

scope.breadth: nouns, verbs, pronouns, story elements, role-play, respectful behavior, writing about story events, discussion protocols
scope.depth: identification and description of story elements and language features; application of role-play and discussion protocols; writing with sentence frames

supports.english_language_learners: Provides rereading of lyrics and text, sentence frames, alternative sentence stems, and visual supports such as word walls and sentence strip chunks.
supports.universal_design_udl: Uses multiple modalities including song, movement, partner talk, role-play, drawing, and writing; offers modified response sheets and seating arrangements for comfort.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Pairs less comfortable singers with more comfortable peers; models writing using familiar texts.
supports.above_level_extend: Encourages students to expand discussion responses and repeat classmates' ideas during Think-Pair-Share.

assessment.method: Observation of student participation in discussions, role-play, and writing tasks; use of checklists for language and speaking/listening progress
assessment.recognition_vs_production: Primarily production through oral and written responses

text_complexity.quantitative: Read-aloud mediation; text pages 11-20 of Summer Sun Risin'
text_complexity.qualitative: Simple narrative structure with clear sequence of events; familiar language and concepts; moderate knowledge demands related to daily life and social behavior
